rich_summary: This passage depicts an extraordinary duel between the teacher Drona and his greatest pupil, Arjuna. Their combat mirrors perfect symmetry: every celestial weapon Drona invokes—Aindra, Pasupata, Vayavya, and others—is countered by Arjuna. Observers compare them to hawks battling in the sky, and even Drona silently praises Arjuna’s mastery, seeing his own training reflected in the student. Heavenly beings gather to witness the spectacle, declaring it beyond ordinary human or divine warfare—like Rudra fighting himself. When Drona unleashes the terrifying Brahma weapon, nature itself trembles, but Arjuna neutralizes it with one of his own. The stalemate dissolves into broader battle. In the next clash, Dhrishtadyumna drives back Duhsasana and advances toward Drona while Nakula and Sahadeva shield him. Amid intense combat, the warriors deliberately avoid unfair weapons, emphasizing a code of righteous warfare even within carnage.

highlight_spans.why: The opening description frames the duel and introduces the awe of the watching warriors.
The comparison of Drona and Arjuna to hawks fighting in the sky captures the intensity and symmetry of their struggle.
Drona internally praises Arjuna, revealing the deep teacher‑student bond beneath the battlefield conflict.
The invocation of the Brahma weapon and the trembling of nature mark the duel’s most cosmic and dangerous moment.
The warriors’ refusal to use unfair weapons highlights the ethical code of dharma guiding the battle.

top_scenes.scene_text: Drona and Arjuna circling each other in chariots while celestial weapons streak across the sky like blazing comets.
Sages, Gandharvas, and gods crowd the darkened sky watching the duel as if witnessing Rudra fighting himself.
Drona unleashes the Brahma weapon as winds roar, seas swell, and Arjuna raises his own radiant counter-weapon to calm the shaking world.
